Title: Cancel an order and verify structured API response wrapper format
Preconditions: An order with numeric ID 101 exists in the system and all its items are in MEASUREMENT_DONE status.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders/101/cancel.

Test Data: Order ID: 101
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with JSON body containing status 'success', message 'Order and all items cancelled successfully.', data null, and meta null.

Title: Upload a Base64 photo using updated payload field 'photo' and optional 'imageName'
Preconditions: The photo storage service is active.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON object containing 'url' and 'objectName', where 'objectName' starts with 'fabric-sample-'.

Title: Retrieve stored file using bucket name and multi-segment object path
Preconditions: A file named 'cloth-101.jpg' exists in storage under the bucket 'customer-photos' inside folder 'customers'.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /customer-photos/customers/cloth-101.jpg.

Test Data: Path: /customer-photos/customers/cloth-101.jpg
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response containing the binary stream of the requested photo.

Title: Attempt to upload a base64 photo with missing or blank photo field
Preconditions: The service is operational and configured with MinIO temp storage.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with JSON body {"error": "Photo is required"}.

Title: Attempt to cancel an order where an order item is not in MEASUREMENT_DONE state
Preconditions: An order exists with ID 101, but at least one of its items has progressed past MEASUREMENT_DONE (for example, to CUTTING_DONE or DELIVERED).
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders/101/cancel.

Test Data: orderId = 101
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with JSON response body containing {"status": "error", "message": "Order can only be cancelled if all items are in MEASUREMENT_DONE state.", "data": null, "meta": null}.

Title: Attempt to upload an empty file via file upload endpoint
Preconditions: The photo upload API endpoint is available.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/photos/upload passing a multipart form parameter 'file' with an empty content (0 bytes).

Test Data: file = empty multipart file (0 bytes)
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with JSON body {"error": "File must not be empty"}.

Title: Attempt to create an order with a measurement group that has missing or blank cloth photo
Expected Result: The system rejects the order creation request and returns an error indicating that a cloth photo is required for the measurement group.

Title: Cancel order with single item boundary where item is in MEASUREMENT_DONE state
Preconditions: An order with ID 101 exists in the system with exactly one item in MEASUREMENT_DONE status.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders/101/cancel.

Test Data: orderId = 101
Expected Result: The system responds with an HTTP 200 OK status code and a JSON ApiResponse object containing 'status': 'success', 'message': 'Order and all items cancelled successfully.', 'data': null, and 'meta': null.

Title: Upload base64 photo with optional imageName parameter provided
Preconditions: The photo upload service is available.
Expected Result: The system responds with HTTP 200 OK and a JSON object containing 'url' and 'objectName', where 'objectName' begins with 'custom-cloth-prefix-' followed by a UUID and the '.jpg' extension.

Title: Retrieve proxied file using multi-level nested object subpath
Preconditions: A file named 'cloth-sample.jpg' exists in the temp bucket under a multi-segment object path 'customers/subfolder/cloth-sample.jpg'.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /temp-photos/customers/subfolder/cloth-sample.jpg (where 'temp-photos' corresponds to the configured temp bucket name).

Test Data: bucket = temp-photos, object path = customers/subfolder/cloth-sample.jpg
Expected Result: The system responds with HTTP 200 OK and streams the binary image resource from the resolved bucket and nested object path.

Title: Verify that file proxy requests specifying unconfigured or arbitrary bucket names are rejected
Preconditions: The file proxy endpoint is active with configured allowed buckets for orders, customers, and temporary storage.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /system-config/keys.txt where system-config is not one of the allowed configured bucket names.

Test Data: Path parameter bucket: system-config, object path: keys.txt
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found). No data is returned and no internal bucket or system error details are exposed.

Title: Upload a Base64-encoded image with custom image name to temp storage
Preconditions: The application service is running and connected to MinIO.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK status code with a JSON payload containing 'url' and 'objectName' (starting with 'profile-sketch-').

Title: Cancel an order and receive formatted ApiResponse response body
Preconditions: An active order exists in the system with orderId 101.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders/101/cancel with an empty body. 2. Check the response status and structure.

Test Data: Path variable orderId = 101
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body matching ApiResponse structure: {"status": "success", "message": "Order and all items cancelled successfully.", "data": null, "meta": null}.

Title: Retrieve a stored image file from nested bucket path through proxy
Preconditions: An object exists in MinIO under customer-photos bucket at path 'customers/cloth-sample.jpg'.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /customer-photos/customers/cloth-sample.jpg. 2. Verify the response stream and headers.

Test Data: Path variable bucket = customer-photos, wildcards = customers/cloth-sample.jpg
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK status code with file stream payload and correct media type headers.

Title: Verify order photo upload stores file in the newly configured order-photos bucket
Preconditions: Application deployed with updated application.properties where minio.order-bucket-name=order-photos. MinIO service running and 'order-photos' bucket exists.
Steps:
1. Start the application with the updated config. 2. Upload an order photo via the order photo API. 3. Inspect MinIO storage or retrieve object path details.

Test Data: Old key: minio.bucket-name=tailor-photos -> New key: minio.order-bucket-name=order-photos
Expected Result: The uploaded order photo is successfully placed into the 'order-photos' bucket without errors.

Title: Verify customer photo upload stores file in the newly configured customer-photos bucket
Preconditions: Application deployed with updated application.properties where minio.customer-bucket-name=customer-photos. MinIO service running and 'customer-photos' bucket exists.
Steps:
1. Start the application with the updated config. 2. Upload a customer profile or reference photo via the customer API. 3. Inspect MinIO storage or response object path.

Test Data: New key: minio.customer-bucket-name=customer-photos
Expected Result: The uploaded customer photo is stored in the 'customer-photos' bucket and a valid presigned URL or path is generated.

Title: Verify temporary uploads write to the newly configured tailor-photos-temp bucket
Preconditions: Application deployed with updated application.properties where minio.temp-bucket-name=tailor-photos-temp. MinIO service running and 'tailor-photos-temp' bucket exists.
Steps:
1. Start the application with the updated config. 2. Perform a temporary photo staging or draft upload operation. 3. Verify file placement in MinIO.

Test Data: Old bucket: tailor-photos -> New key: minio.temp-bucket-name=tailor-photos-temp
Expected Result: Temporary photos are uploaded and isolated in the 'tailor-photos-temp' bucket successfully.
